variables.effect: available() returns false for the whole process. Software attention then uses the AVX-512 loop for every KV page. It is ON in the deb preset (CMakePresets.json:68) and in the CMake CI job (.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml:355). In a build without the option the variable is never read. There is no command-line flag. The value cannot change while the process runs.
variables.how_to_check: No log line prints the value. The FUSE stats file /model/<model id>/attention/summary has the fields amx_compiled and amx_available (h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:727-731; filled at h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:478-479). amx_compiled true with amx_available false means that the variable is 1 or that the host has no usable AMX. The file exists also when TRON_ATTN_STATS is off (h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:934), but only when FUSE stats are initialized (h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:916). With TRON_ATTN_STATS=1 the same summary is printed to stderr when the model state is destroyed (h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:829-830).
variables.audience_reason: The source calls it a switch for emergency disable and rollback of the AMX path (src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:86, h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:47-50), and the packaged deb build contains it.

The process logs the error line TRON_ASSERT(valid): invalid TRON_ATTN_SECTION_SPLIT '<text>'; expected a nonnegative integer, then calls std::abort (h/common/assert.hpp:57-63 and :69-74). The planner picks the smallest piece count whose predicted finish time is at least 10% better than no split (h/tron/models/model.hpp:3328-3338).

variables.audience_reason: It tunes the speed of software attention in rinzler and runtron.
variables.disagreement: Vague, not wrong. The inventory says that a bad value makes the process abort 'on first use'. It does not say when first use is. The code reads the variable in finish_sw_plan (h/tron/models/model.hpp:3201), after the early return for zero software work (h/tron/models/model.hpp:3167). So a bad value passes program start and model load, and the process aborts at the first forward pass that has software attention work.

variables.invalid_value: Non-numeric text gives 0 (off). No message is logged. This result comes from reading the code. The code was not run.
variables.effect: When the value is above 0, every extend request first calls defrag_books(value) on the token tree node that it extends (src/tron/scheduler/full.cpp:121). The call takes the node and up to value - 1 ancestors. From the oldest to the youngest, it tries to move the KV book of each node into the free end of the book of its parent (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1321-1342 and :1473-1500). A move happens only when the node starts its own book, the parent book ends where the node starts, and the parent book has room.

variables.how_to_check: none found for the value itself. Indirect only: the warning Fragmentation Risk! (src/tron/generation/speculate.cpp:45-47) appears when the width is above 1 and this depth is below the draft tree depth.
variables.audience_reason: It tunes how the KV cache of rinzler and runtron compacts its books.
variables.disagreement: Incomplete on a negative value. The inventory says: 'A negative value wraps to a very large size_t; the code does not reject it.' The inventory also does not say that the same reserve call makes a very large positive value cost 8 bytes x value of reserved memory per extend request. Both points come from reading the code. The code was not run.

It runs when the start location of a generation has a speculator (src/tron/generation.cpp:51-56), that is, with speculative decoding. TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_SIZE prunes the tree to a node count, so a depth above that size has no effect. The value is compared with TRON_DEFRAG_BOOKS_DEPTH for the warning at src/tron/generation/speculate.cpp:43-48 when the width is above 1. No command-line flag.
variables.how_to_check: none found for the value. Indirect only: when a speculative generation ends, the info log line Speculation mean acceptance length = <X> rate = <Y> over <N> tokens (src/tron/generation/speculate.cpp:454-456) gives the mean number of tokens accepted per sampling step.
variables.audience_reason: It tunes the speed of speculative decoding in rinzler and runtron.

readers.program: libpos, the driver for real FPGA cards (rinzler, runtron, hardware tests). Programs built on pos_fake (rinzler_host, rinzler_mock, rinzler_proxy) do not contain this code. Function get_devices
readers.mechanism: call of warm_up_first_result_fault(). It runs in the first call of get_devices, after pos_startup and after the device workers are ready (lines 886-906)

variables.values: Exactly the text 0 skips the warm-up. Any other text leaves it on.
variables.empty_value: The warm-up runs. The empty text is not equal to 0.
variables.invalid_value: Any text other than 0 (for example 1, false, 00, or 0 with a space) leaves the warm-up on. No message is logged.
variables.effect: With 0 the driver skips the first-result warm-up. The warm-up is one throwaway int4 matrix multiply with zero weights on each FPGA card whose PCI device id is 0x0011 or higher (src/pos/driver.cpp:837-853). The note in the source says that on some Archer bitfiles the first int4 weight fetch after an FPGA configuration stores corrupted weights, so the first matmul result is wrong (src/pos/driver.cpp:799-816). So 0 on a deployed system removes a protection.
variables.interactions: No command-line flag. The source says that the fault detector test and t_newregs set it to 0 (src/pos/driver.cpp:814-816; t/t_first_result_fault.cpp:51, t/t_newregs.cpp:25).
variables.how_to_check: Info log line at start. Skipped: INIT: first-result warm-up skipped (TRON_FIRST_RESULT_WARMUP=0) (src/pos/driver.cpp:820). Ran: INIT: first-result warm-up: one int4 matmul on each of <N> device(s) in <X> ms (src/pos/driver.cpp:869-874).
variables.audience_reason: Product code reads it, but only two tests need the value 0. On a deployed system the value 0 can let a wrong first result through.

variables.name: TRON_GOLDEN_TOKENS

readers.program: rinzler_proxy (shared library proxy_scheduler). Function tron::proxy::load_golden_map_from_env
readers.mechanism: std::getenv. The text is used as a file name for std::ifstream (line 313)

readers.program: rinzler_proxy (shared library proxy_scheduler). Function stream_generate of the proxy scheduler
readers.mechanism: call of proxy::load_golden_map_from_env(), once per generation. A restart of a generation also calls it

variables.values: Path to a JSON file (the golden map). The top level is an object or an array (src/tron/scheduler/golden_tokens.cpp:246-279). An object maps a prompt key, which is a comma-separated list of token ids, to the tokens that the proxy emits. The reserved keys are default and rendered_at. An array is used as the default entry. The full format is at h/tron/scheduler/golden_tokens.hpp:102-116.
variables.default: Unset: the loader logs the error proxy: TRON_GOLDEN_TOKENS unset; every generation will throw until it is set to a file with a non-empty "default" (src/tron/scheduler/golden_tokens.cpp:303 and :309-312). stream_generate then throws std::runtime_error proxy: golden map unavailable: <cause> (src/tron/scheduler/proxy.cpp:414-415). The process keeps running.
variables.empty_value: The empty text is tried as a file name. The open fails, the loader logs cannot open TRON_GOLDEN_TOKENS file ''; every generation will throw until it is readable (src/tron/scheduler/golden_tokens.cpp:313-317), and each generation throws the same error as for unset.
variables.invalid_value: A file that cannot be opened, is not valid JSON, or has the wrong shape gives one error log line per generation with the cause (src/tron/scheduler/golden_tokens.cpp:313-334) and the same throw. A prompt with no matching key and no default entry throws proxy: no golden tokens for prompt key <key> (src/tron/scheduler/proxy.cpp:515-518). The process keeps running in all these cases.
variables.effect: Names the file from which rinzler_proxy takes the tokens that it emits in place of running a model. The variable and the file are read again for every generation, so a change to the file takes effect at the next request without a restart.
variables.interactions: When the file has a rendered_at entry, RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE must be set to the same text. Otherwise the generation throws (src/tron/scheduler/golden_tokens.cpp:223-244, called at src/tron/scheduler/proxy.cpp:418). Only rinzler_proxy links the proxy scheduler (src/CMakeLists.txt:180-190). No command-line flag.
variables.how_to_check: Info log line for each generation: proxy: prompt key <key> -> <N> golden tokens (src/tron/scheduler/proxy.cpp:504). A failed load logs proxy: <cause> at error level (src/tron/scheduler/golden_tokens.cpp:303).
variables.audience_reason: It is the main input of rinzler_proxy. The task lists rinzler_proxy as a deployed program and CMake installs it (src/CMakeLists.txt:196). In practice rinzler_proxy is test equipment, so test is also defensible.

variables.name: TRON_HEAP_PROFILE_PATH

readers.program: libsystem, function pos_heap_v2::dump_profile. The arena heap exists only after the startup of libpos (rinzler, runtron, hardware tests)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv. The read comes after the check that the shadow map is on (line 914). The only product caller is the out-of-memory path of pos_heap_v2::allocate (src/system/heap_v2.cpp:523)

readers.program: libsystem, function pos_heap::dump_profile of the legacy heap. It is compiled only when the macro HEAP_SHADOW is defined. The macro is commented out at h/system/heap.hpp:20 and no build file defines it
readers.mechanism: std::getenv

variables.values: Path of a file. The file is opened with fopen in append mode (src/system/heap_v2.cpp:949).
variables.empty_value: Not the same as unset. The histogram is built, the open of the empty path fails, and the warning heap_v2::dump_profile: could not open <path> for append is logged (src/system/heap_v2.cpp:949-953).
variables.invalid_value: A path that cannot be opened for append gives the same warning. The program continues.
variables.effect: When the arena allocator cannot serve an allocation from the DMA heap, it appends a text histogram of the live allocations to this file. The histogram is grouped by size class and by caller address. Each block starts with === OOM n_live=<count> === (src/system/heap_v2.cpp:956).
variables.interactions: Nothing is written unless the shadow map is on (TRON_HEAP_SHADOW=1 or --heap-shadow). The arena allocator must be in use: TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR unset with the build default ON (src/system/CMakeLists.txt:86-88), or set to 1. Each dump is appended, so the file grows. The caller addresses are raw. The source says to resolve them with addr2line (src/system/heap.cpp:210-213).
variables.how_to_check: No log line prints the path. The warning at src/system/heap_v2.cpp:951 shows a path that cannot be opened. A successful dump adds a block that starts with === OOM n_live= to the file.
variables.audience_reason: It is a diagnostic dump for heap fragmentation research (h/system/heap_v2.hpp:6-10). It needs the shadow map, which is off by default.

variables.name: TRON_HEAP_SHADOW

readers.program: libsystem, function read_heap_shadow_env. It is reached only through the startup of libpos (rinzler, runtron, hardware tests)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv, then strcmp with the text 1 (line 108)

readers.program: libsystem, function pos_heap_setup. pos_startup_host of libpos calls it (src/pos/driver.cpp:290). The fake pos_startup_host does not (src/pos/fake.cpp:91-124)
readers.mechanism: call of read_heap_shadow_env(), joined with the --heap-shadow flag by a logical OR. The call runs only when the arena allocator is selected (line 175)

variables.values: Exactly the text 1 turns the shadow map on. The code compares the text with strcmp.
variables.default: Unset: off, unless the option --heap-shadow is given.
variables.empty_value: Off. The empty text is not equal to 1.
variables.invalid_value: Any text other than 1 (for example true, yes, 0) is off. No message is logged.
variables.effect: The arena allocator (pos_heap_v2) keeps one record for each live DMA allocation: the requested size, the slot size, the size class and two caller addresses (src/system/heap_v2.cpp:213-217). When memory is freed it checks the pointer and the exact size. A mismatch fails TRON_ASSERT and the process aborts (src/system/heap_v2.cpp:243-251). The records also feed the profile dump of TRON_HEAP_PROFILE_PATH.
variables.interactions: The system option --heap-shadow does the same (src/system/system.cpp:2044-2045). runtron passes its own --heap-shadow flag on (src/runtron.cpp:646-647). The same parser reads the SYSTEM_CONFIG text (src/system/system.cpp:2112-2118). The result is variable OR flag (src/system/memory.cpp:180-181), so the variable cannot turn the flag off. It has no effect with the legacy heap, that is, when TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR is set to a text other than 1 (src/system/memory.cpp:93-97 and :175). The value is fixed when the heap is created. Cost, from the source comment: one map entry per live allocation, about 750 000 entries at the measured peak (h/system/heap_v2.hpp:13-18).
variables.how_to_check: Info log line at heap setup: pos_heap_setup: using arena allocator (pos_heap_v2) with shadow map (src/system/memory.cpp:182-183). Without the shadow map the line ends after (pos_heap_v2).
variables.audience_reason: It is a diagnostic for heap research and leak checks. It adds a cost per allocation, and the tests are the only setters in this checkout.

notes: Method. Step 1 was done from the code only, before the inventory files were opened. Nothing in the checkout was built or run. So every statement about an empty or invalid value comes from reading the code and from the C++ standard library rules. Three results depend on library rules and were not run: std::stof throwing inside noexcept callers (TRON_BOOK_GROWTH_FACTOR), std::vector::reserve throwing std::length_error for a negative depth (TRON_DEFRAG_BOOKS_DEPTH), and std::atoi on numbers above the int range (marked not determined). A test run would confirm them. Result. The inventory agrees with the code on 10 of 14 variables. It is vague or incomplete on 4: TRON_DEFRAG_BOOKS_DEPTH (a negative value terminates the process), TRON_BOOK_GROWTH_FACTOR (a bad value terminates the process, and only later, during a request), TRON_ATTN_SECTION_SPLIT (the abort for a bad value comes at the first forward pass with software attention work, not at start), TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_WIDTH (the effect of 0 is not stated). No inventory statement was found to be false. Every site that the inventory cites for these 14 variables was opened and it matches. Additions that are not disagreements. The field how_to_check is new for all 14. The log line for TRON_HEAP_SHADOW (src/system/memory.cpp:182-183) is not in the inventory. With the shadow map on, a free with a wrong size or an unknown pointer aborts the process (src/system/heap_v2.cpp:243-251). The inventory says only that the map 'allows an exact size check'. Merge note. The two inventory files give different 'when' text for TRON_FIRST_RESULT_WARMUP and TRON_HEAP_SHADOW ('every call of ...' in cpp-pos-system, 'once at startup' in cpp-rinzler-runtron). Both describe the same single read per driver startup. Missing variables. Every getenv call in the 13 product files read for this task was checked against the three inventory files. All names are present. Related fact for the document as a whole. The comment at h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:50-51 says that TRON_AMX_DISABLE 'will be listed in the TRON environment-variable document' and names the issue https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/issues/4338. Documents. doc/pos_heap_v2.md:781 says the shadow map is on when TRON_HEAP_SHADOW is 'set'. The code needs exactly the text 1 (src/system/memory.cpp:108).
